name: Liquidation Feed
note: Live perp liquidation tape. New prints drop in from the top with a side-tinted flash, older rows dim as they age, and the 24h notional counter tweens on every hit. Long liquidations are forced sells (red, down arrow), shorts are forced buys (green, up arrow). The ticker pauses itself in a hidden tab and stops when the node is removed.

name: AMM Depth Curve
note: Constant-product pool drawn as x*y=k. The curve strokes itself in on mount; dragging the size slider walks the reserve marker down the curve, shades the slippage region between spot and execution, and recomputes realised price impact from the actual reserve maths (1200 ETH / 4.05M USDC).
html:

name: Bridge Confirmations
note: Cross-chain transfer running its real lifecycle: lock, twelve source confirmations counted one by one against a filling rail, relay, then mint on the destination. Each cleared hop draws its own checkmark, the live hop keeps a pulsing ring, and the status line is a polite live region. Loops so the whole sequence is visible.

name: On-Chain Order Book
note: Six-level ladder with cumulative depth bars that grow in from the right. Resting-size changes flash the level that was touched, and when the mid moves it repaints with a directional arrow and a green or red pulse. Prices, sizes and totals are tabular so the columns never jitter; the feed idles in a hidden tab.

name: Yield Comparison Table
note: Sortable DeFi yield table in a real table element. Clicking a header re-ranks the pools and the rows physically slide to their new positions with a FLIP transform, so you can follow a pool as it moves. APY gauges sweep out and the figures count up on mount; aria-sort, header buttons and focus rings keep it keyboard-usable.

name: Wallet Connect States
note: The whole connect handshake as an explicit state machine: detect, approve, sign, ready, with a rejection branch that lands on error 4001 and offers retry. A progress rail advances between states, the panel swaps colour and spinner, and a live region announces each transition. Roughly one attempt in four is rejected so the error path is reachable.

name: Impermanent Loss Calculator
note: Divergence-loss calculator on a $10,000 50/50 position. The loss curve draws itself in on mount, then each preset move springs the marker along the real 2*sqrt(r)/(1+r)-1 curve with a velocity tween rather than a CSS transition, while the headline figure and the LP-versus-HODL bars ease to their new values.
